brief: Democrats swept both chambers in the midterms (Senate 54 seats vs 44 Republican, +7; House 253 vs 157, +41), which AP called as of 6 November. AHAM attributes the result to voter dissatisfaction with the Iran war and rising living costs; VP JD Vance called it a rebuke of the administration's record rather than an endorsement of Democrats. Divided government from January 2027 narrows Trump's path on tax and spending without bipartisan support, while Democrats lack the 60 votes to advance their own agenda or the two-thirds to override a veto, so AHAM expects the White House to lean more on executive action and foreign policy. Separately, data centres became a campaign issue over electricity bills, water use and limited job creation. AHAM judges a broad federal AI ban unlikely given competitiveness with China, but sees tighter state-level regulation, especially after Democratic wins in Texas and Ohio, as the nearer-term risk that could raise costs and delay projects short term while supporting a more sustainable buildout over time. Combined Meta/Alphabet/Microsoft/Amazon capex reached ~USD202bn in Q3 2026 against negative USD26bn free cash flow, and a record USD15bn October leveraged-ETF inflow amplified the selloff once sentiment reversed. AHAM has trimmed technology hardware exposure further and remains underweight pending clarity on state policy and hyperscaler funding.
